articles.text: NǍINAI: Xiǎolán, kàn bào na!
GRANDMOTHER: Reading the paper, Xiǎolán?
XIǍOLÁN: Nǎinai, jīntian bàoshang shuōle, "Yíge zuì hǎo, liǎngge gòu le, sānge tài duō"!
XIǍOLÁN: Grandma, today it says in the paper, "One is best, two are enough, three are too many"!
NǍINAI: Shénme? "Yíge zuì hǎo"? Wǒ méi tīngmíngbai.
GRANDMOTHER: What? "One is best"? I don't understand.
XIǍOLÁN: Nà shi shuō shēng háizi, shēng yíge zuì hǎo, liǎngge jiù gòu le, sānge tài duō.
XIǍOLÁN: It's about having children. It's best to have one, two are enough, and three are too many.
NǍINAI: "Shēng yíge zuì hǎo"? Shēng ge nǚháizi zěnme bàn? Hái děi zài shēng yíge nánde ma!
GRANDMOTHER: "It's best to have one"? What do you do if you have a girl? Then you have to try to have a boy!
XIǍOLÁN: Ēi, nǎinai, nǚháizi yǒu shénme bù hǎo? Nánháizi yě hǎo, nǚháizi yě hǎo, dōu shi zìjǐde háizi ya!
XIǍOLÁN: But Grandma, what's wrong with girls? Boys or girls, they're all one's own children!
NǍINAI: Nà bù yíyàng. Nǚháizi jiéle hūn, shēngle háizi, háizi děi xìng zhàngfude xìngr. Nǐ xiǎng nánháizi hé nǚháizi yíyàng ma?
GRANDMOTHER: It's not the same thing. When a girl gets married and has a child, the child has to take the husband's surname. You think boys are the same as girls?
XIǍOLÁN: Nà wǒ bù tóngyì. Nín yě shi nǚde, nín wèishénme nàme kànbuqǐ fùnǚ a?
XIǍOLÁN: That I don't agree with. You're a woman too. Why do you look down on women so much?
NǍINAI: Bú shi kànbuqǐ, shèhuìde qíngxing jiù shi zhèiyàngr. Nǐ yéye xìng Zhāng, wǒ zìjǐ xìng Lǐ, jiéhūn yǐhòu rénjia jiào wǒ Zhāng Lǐ Shì, zěnme méiyou rén jiào wǒ Lǐ Zhāng Shì?

GRANDMOTHER: It's not that I look down on them. That's the way society is. Your grandfather's name is Zhāng and mine is Lǐ. After we got married people called me Zhāng Lǐ Shì. Why didn't anyone call me Lǐ Zhāng Shì!
XIǍOLÁN: Zhèi shi jiù fēngsú, xiànzài méiyou zhèixiē shuōfǎr le. Wǒ shi Zhāng Xiǎolán, jiéhūn yǐhòu wǒ hái shi Zhāng Xiǎolán.
XIǍOLÁN: That's the old custom. Those terms aren't used anymore. I'm Zhāng Xiǎolán, and after I get married I'll still be Zhāng Xiǎolán.
NǍINAI: Yǐhòu háizi yě xìng Zhāng ma?
GRANDMOTHER: And will your children use the surname Zhāng too?

XIǍOLÁN: Zěnme bù kěyi? Nín kàn duìmiànrde Wáng Āyí, yǒule háizi jiào Wáng Lín, yě méiyou rén shuō bù kěyi ma! Zài shuō, duō shēng háizi yǒu shénme hǎochur? Dàjiā shōurù dōu bù duō, háizi duōle, dàren duō kǔ!

XIǍOLÁN: Why not? Look at Auntie Wáng across the way. When she had her child it was called Wáng Lín, and no one said there was anything wrong with that. Besides, what's the advantage in having a lot of children? Everyone has a small income, and if there are a lot of children, how hard it is for the adults!
NǍINAI: Hǎole, hǎole, jiù suàn nǐ shuōde duì. Kuài chī fàn ba! Chīwánle hái děi shàng xué qu na!
GRANDMOTHER: Okay, okay, let's say you're right. Hurry up and eat! You have to go to school after you finish eating!
